subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a general temp-artifact provenance and cleanup model, or should core only cover runtime-critical temp-path guardrails plus a minimal plugin/skill seam?
rationale: The issue is valid but the storage owner, cleanup authority, and boundary between core safety checks and workflow-specific janitor behavior require maintainer product intent before implementation.

options.title: Core guardrails plus minimal provenance seam
options.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a SQLite-backed provenance contract for OpenClaw-owned artifacts, while workflow-specific classifications live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core provenance registry
options.body: Core would own artifact classification and cleanup policy for all first-class OpenClaw temp artifacts, accepting broader state and janitor responsibility.

options.title: Plugin or skill-only workflow
options.body: Artifact provenance would stay outside core except for concrete bugs, with janitor/classification workflows published through ClawHub.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus minimal provenance seam
recommendation.body: Core would cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a SQLite-backed provenance contract for OpenClaw-owned artifacts, while workflow-specific classifications live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses core safety defaults, storage policy, and plugin/ClawHub scope, and steipete has the strongest combined history in those areas.
